title: E-Math mensuration: sectors, pyramids and spheres
subject: math

objectives.text: Find arc lengths and sector areas as fractions of a full circle
successCriteria: I can write the sector fraction as angle over 360 and apply the same fraction to 2 pi r and to pi r squared
I can find the arc length 2 pi and sector area 6 pi for a 60 degree sector of radius 6 cm
assessmentPoints: Arc and sector answers in the opening activity
Partner explanations of the angle fraction

objectives.text: Calculate the volume of a pyramid from its base area and vertical height
successCriteria: I can say three identical pyramids fill the prism on the same base with the same height
I can calculate 1/3 x 36 x 4 = 48 cubic centimetres for a square pyramid with base 6 cm by 6 cm and vertical height 4 cm
assessmentPoints: Pyramid answers in the second activity
Worksheet answers checked against the trap in the fourth activity

objectives.text: Use the sphere volume formula and explain why area scales with r squared
successCriteria: I can state the sphere volume as 4/3 pi r cubed and calculate 36 pi for r = 3 cm
I can explain that doubling the radius quadruples the area, from 9 pi to 36 pi, because area scales with r squared
assessmentPoints: Sphere answers in the third activity
Trap answers in the closing exit ticket

differentiation.support: Provide the student notes worked example open at the sector step so learners can follow the 60/360 = 1/6 fraction before trying the sphere calculation themselves.

activities.title: A common mistake: doubling r doubles area

differentiation.stretch: Ask learners to explain why four radius-3 disks tile the radius-6 disk exactly before checking the squared-paper count.
